title: The North Face Rock 32 review: roomy for two, snug for three
dek: A three-pole, two-door tent with big vestibules and an all-mesh body. Owners love the space and setup, and disagree on waterproofing.
subject: The North Face Rock 32
verdict: The Rock 32 gives two people lots of room, or three people a snug fit, with two doors and large vestibules and a quick, easy pitch. Owners are split on waterproofing and durability, and the floor is thin, so put a footprint under it and check the coatings on a used one.
bestFor: Two people who want space, or three on summer trips, mostly car camping or short hikes.
notFor: Cold-weather camping, tall campers over about 6 feet 2, or rough ground without a footprint.
pros: Roomy for two, with two doors and large vestibules
Pitches in about 5 to 10 minutes, even solo
All-mesh body breathes well and gives a wide view
cons: Mixed waterproofing reports; fly can touch the mesh in heavy rain
Thin floor benefits from a footprint
Retains little heat, so it's mainly a summer tent
One 6'3" owner found it too short
body:
## The short version

The Rock 32 is the three-person version of the Rock: three 9 mm poles, two doors, big vestibules and an all-mesh body. Owners on Trailspace praise the space and the quick pitch, and disagree on how well it keeps out heavy rain.

## Space

It fits two comfortably, and reviewers call it a snug three-person tent. One owner at 6 foot 3 found it too short.

## Weather

Many owners stayed dry through heavy, multi-day storms. Others reported leaks, including one whose floor soaked through and one who had to re-waterproof the floor. One owner found the fly touches the mesh walls in heavy rain, which lets water through. Pitch the fly tight and use every guyline.

## Setup and weight

Most owners say it's up in 5 to 10 minutes, and one person can manage it. At about 5 to 6.5 pounds it's heavy for solo backpacking but manageable when two people split it.

## Durability

Owners report anything from no tears after five years to expecting major repairs within three. The common thread is the thin floor: use a footprint. The mesh is also easy for animals to damage.

## Poles and parts

The Rock 32 uses **3 poles**, **9 mm** tubing.

The North Face doesn't publish pole lengths. To match a replacement, lay your pole out straight, measure tip to tip, count the sections, and read the diameter printed near a joint (or use calipers). Then search the Rock 32 in our [pole and parts finder](/poles?model=Rock%2032), compare against measured stock in the [pole size chart](/poles/sizes), or search by measurement in [find a pole by size](/poles/size).

## Bottom line

For summer trips with two people who want space, the Rock 32 is a comfortable, easy tent. Check the floor and fly coatings on a used one, and add a footprint.
